name: ax
one_liner: A Kubernetes-style control system for running huge numbers of AI agent tasks in locked-down sandboxes at once, built by Google.
buyer: A platform or infrastructure engineer at a company that needs to run many autonomous coding or automation agents safely and cheaply at scale.
business_use_cases: An AI-powered QA company uses ax to spin up thousands of isolated test-running agents per day, each with locked-down network access.
A dev-tools startup builds a 'run any coding agent in the cloud' product on top of ax instead of building its own orchestrator.
An enterprise security team uses ax's Gateway feature to enforce that internal agents can only reach an approved allowlist of hosts.

money_ideas.idea: Offer managed 'ax-as-a-service' hosting for companies that want agent orchestration without running their own Kubernetes cluster.
Consulting to help enterprises adopt ax's security/gateway model for compliance-sensitive agent deployments.

steal_this: The README flags major breaking changes before a stable release, so the honest move is to watch this one, not build a paid product on it yet — it's not a weekend project today.
